subject: Transportation Systems
title: Station Design Basics
description: A 60-second lesson on Station Design Basics.

hook.text: A subway station isn't just a hole in the ground. It's a machine designed to move thousands per hour.

buildup.text: Platform width, staircase placement, and ceiling height all affect how quickly passengers flow.

discovery.text: Engineers model crowd movement like fluid dynamics—people flow like water through bottlenecks.

twist.text: A poorly placed pillar can cut throughput by 20%. Every detail matters at rush hour.

climax.text: The best stations feel effortless. That ease is the result of obsessive engineering.

punchline.text: Good station design is invisible. Bad design causes stampedes.

quiz.question: How do engineers model passenger movement in stations?
